brief: Deep, measured documentary narrator. Calm authority, never ad-read. The narrator explains; they do not hype.

primary.why: Deep, natural, articulate, believable — middle-aged US male. Closest catalogue match to the documentary brief, and it reads as trustworthy rather than sold-to.
primary.model_note: Direct ElevenLabs, not routed through GMICloud — 'ElevenLabs-TTS-v3' is the GMI slug and is rejected here. Going direct also gives the run two distinct provider adapters rather than one.

fallback.why: Narrative-classified, calm, US male. Nearest tonal match on the fallback provider.
fallback.note: A fallback voice will never match the primary exactly. That is disclosed rather than hidden: the manifest records which provider voiced each block and the receipt shows it. A visible substitution is more honest than a silent one.

delivery.what_the_data_says: Word count is a poor predictor: 22 words ran 8.96s while 26 words ran 8.88s — more words, shorter take. Rate varied 2.22-2.93 w/s across four takes. The only take that landed in window was the CHOPPY one, at 22 words across five sentences.
delivery.reverses_the_imported_guidance: vox-motion-graphics says 'prefer single flowing sentences' because flowing lines run FAST and overrun. On eleven_v3 with this voice the opposite holds: flowing lines run short and it is sentence-end pauses that fill the ten-second window. The skill's 20-24 word rule was calibrated on Higgsfield seed_audio, a slower voice. Ours needs 23-27 words across 2-3 sentences.
delivery.duration_must_be_measured: asset.duration comes back None from the ElevenLabs adapter, so POL-5 cannot read it from the manifest. Take length is measured with ffprobe on the downloaded file. Word count is only a coarse pre-flight bound; the measured take is the enforcement.

measured_2026_07_28_narration.what: Six CS-1 blocks voiced end to end on Marcus Louis / eleven_v3, silence stripped, ffprobe on the trimmed file. MOO-426.

takes.result: IN WINDOW after one [pause] correction, from 7.62s

measured_2026_07_28_narration.the_two_windows_disagree: POL-5 admits 23-27 words. On this narrator that produced 9.25-12.56s across six blocks, against a 9.0-10.5s take window — so three of six missed, all by running long, and no correction can reach them. This is not the takes being wrong; it is two published numbers that were calibrated separately. EDITORIAL DECISION OUTSTANDING: widen target_take_seconds to about 9.0-12.5s and accept a ~65s piece, or narrow POL-5 to about 22-25 words and accept shorter blocks. Left unchanged here because it is an editor's call, not an engineer's.
measured_2026_07_28_narration.pause_tags_work_and_are_measured: eleven_v3 does not accept SSML <break> — ElevenLabs documents break tags on every model EXCEPT v3, and audio tags on v3 instead. [pause] buys about 0.36s at each internal sentence boundary and [long pause] about 1.25s; the tags are interpreted, not spoken, which silencedetect confirms rather than duration alone. See scripts/spike_pause_tag.py.
measured_2026_07_28_narration.short_pause_was_dropped: [short pause] was in the ladder by symmetry and never by measurement. Block 6 spent both corrections on it against a 0.26s deficit and moved a tenth of a second; one [pause] then moved it 1.63s and landed it. v3's audio tags are probabilistic, so the smallest notch is the one most likely to be ignored.
measured_2026_07_28_narration.lmnt_pads_heavily: The CS-5 sabotage run measured LMNT emitting up to 28.7s of trailing silence on one block — 40.08s raw, 11.35s of words. Stripping silence before measuring is not tidiness on this fallback; without it that block would have been forty seconds long in the assembly.
measured_2026_07_28_narration.do_not_voice_six_blocks_at_once: Six concurrent ElevenLabs calls returned code=rate_limit and pushed four of six blocks onto LMNT. A narrator change we caused ourselves, recorded as though the provider had failed. Two at a time.

correction_order: lengthen with [pause] tags at internal sentence boundaries — the only lever that leaves the journalist's words alone

SUPERSEDED 2026-07-28: 'lower speech rate one notch'. Unreachable. The genblaze ElevenLabs adapter builds voice_settings from stability, similarity_boost and style only, and never forwards speed. An overrun therefore has no correction at all and is flagged immediately rather than re-rendered: four long blocks on the live run got two fresh renders each and one of the eight landed, for about $0.25 and a one-second change in runtime.
flag for human review after two attempts
delivery.why_not_shorter: SUPERSEDED 2026-07-28. This read: 'A short take is worse than a slight overrun. The assembler centres short takes, so a 7s take starts about 1.5s late and reads as desync; a slight overrun is speed-compressed pitch-safely and passes unnoticed.' Both halves described an assembler that no longer exists. Centring a take in a fixed ten-second block puts dead air at both ends of every block, so a short take was only the visible symptom of the window itself. Design spec 6.6 replaces it: block length is derived from the take (0.4s lead-in + take + a 0.5-1.5s tail), the clip is trimmed or its last frame held to match, and the voice is never speed-compressed. A short take now costs runtime, not sync.

assembly_contract.measure_with: ffprobe on the downloaded file — asset.duration is None from the ElevenLabs adapter
never: speed-compress the voice to fit a window
stretch or squeeze video to fit audio
centre a take inside a fixed block
assembly_contract.why: Audio leads and picture follows. Narration on the cut means the shot is never seen; narration centred in a fixed window means dead air at both ends. 0.4s of lead-in is the beat a viewer needs to read a new image before a voice starts.

delivery.pol5_role: POL-5's window is now a RUNTIME BUDGET, not a sync constraint. Six takes near ten seconds keeps the piece around sixty. A take outside the window no longer desyncs anything — it makes the story longer or shorter than intended.
